title: Protective Glass Breakage
introduction: Protective glass breakage is the failure of the front cover glass of a PV module through cracking or shattering. The cover glass serves as the primary mechanical and environmental protection for the cells and encapsulant layers beneath it. When transport impacts, installation errors, hail, or other mechanical loads exceed the fracture strength of the brittle glass, it shatters or cracks. Broken glass immediately eliminates the module's primary moisture and mechanical barrier, allowing water vapor to reach the cells and creating safety hazards. Hotspot formation is also exacerbated by broken glass by allowing greater current mismatch.
reasoning: The 1217-MDPI PV failure review documents glass shattering from poor transportation and manufacturing as a recognized PV module failure that enables moisture ingress and contributes to hotspot formation.

key_findings.claim: Glass shattering results from poor transportation or incorrect manufacturing processes
key_findings.detail: Glass shattering in PV modules can result from poor transportation or incorrect manufacturing processes. [^mdpi1217a] Hotspot failures are not only driven by broken glass but also by shading and mismatch failures, indicating that glass breakage is a co-contributor to multiple downstream failure modes. [^mdpi1217b]

key_findings.detail: Shattering or breakage of the module's glass allows water vapor to enter the solar cells. [^mdpi1217c] This moisture ingress creates short circuits and safety risks including electrical shock, while also enabling corrosion of internal metal conductors.
